<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תשרי_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518913771_theRebbe_98" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_A9_D7_A8_D7_99_meluket__BH_POST_1766518913771_theRebbe_98__p004">
  <section v="9">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the oath is in Binah, Yesod, and Malchus, connecting to the Tzemach Tzedek's teaching that Binah reveals Atik, and Malchus relates to the oath's power to influence the soul in the body.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this can be connected with what the Tzemach Tzedek said,</t>
    <t s="1">that an oath is in Binah, in Yesod, and in Malchus,</t>
    <t s="2">for this that an oath is in Binah relates to the oath itself,</t>
    <t s="3">the drawing down of Atik</t>
    <t s="4">[and similarly the drawing down of the root of the soul],</t>
    <t s="5">for in Binah there is the revelation of Atik.</t>
    <t s="6">As it is said,</t>
    <t s="7">"And a river goes out from Eden,"</t>
    <t s="8">for "river" is Binah and "Eden" is Atik,</t>
    <t s="9">and the explanation of "a river goes out from Eden" is that in Binah there is the revelation of Atik.</t>
    <t s="10">And this that an oath is in Malchus relates to the satiety of the oath,</t>
    <t s="11">for this that the oath influences and gives power to the soul within the body is through the drawing down being in Malchus,</t>
    <t s="12">and this that an oath is in Yesod,</t>
    <t s="13">it is,</t>
    <t s="14">that the drawing down of Binah</t>
    <t s="15">(and the Atik within it)</t>
    <t s="16">into Malchus is through Yesod.</t>
    <t s="17">And this is also the connection with the third interpretation of "they adjure him" that it is from the word "seven,"</t>
    <t s="18">for according to one explanation this refers to Yesod,</t>
    <t s="19">which is the seventh from Binah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section connects the oath "be righteous" to the seventh month, explaining that man was created on the sixth day to be both after and before Creation, and Rosh Hashanah is called the beginning of Your works because man's purpose began then.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And based on this, the connection of the oath with which they adjure him "be righteous" with the seventh month will be understood,</t>
    <t s="2">the month of the oath,</t>
    <t s="3">for this that the creation of man was on the sixth day of the act of Creation,</t>
    <t s="4">the first day of the seventh month,</t>
    <t s="5">is because of two reasons.</t>
    <t s="6">Because he is after the act of Creation,</t>
    <t s="7">for the root of the still, vegetable, and animal is from Tohu and the root of man is from Tikkun that is below Tohu.</t>
    <t s="8">And because he is before the act of Creation</t>
    <t s="9">(prior in level),</t>
    <t s="10">as it is brought in the Gemara,</t>
    <t s="11">that this that man was created at the end is so that he should enter the feast immediately,</t>
    <t s="12">which indicates the superiority of man,</t>
    <t s="13">that all of Creation is for the sake of man.</t>
    <t s="14">For also the coming into being of Tohu that preceded Tikkun is in order that there should be a refinement of Tohu through the service of man,</t>
    <t s="15">as above.</t>
    <t s="16">And this is what is said about the day of Rosh Hashanah, "This day is the beginning of Your works,"</t>
    <t s="17">even though the creation of the world was on the twenty-fifth of Elul,</t>
    <t s="18">for</t>
    <t s="19">the intention in the creation of the world is that man, through his service, should make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="20">and this matter began on the day man was created.</t>
    <t s="21">For in addition to this that specifically then the possibility to complete this intention was made,</t>
    <t s="22">it was then also done in actuality,</t>
    <t s="23">as our sages, of blessed memory, said</t>
    <t s="24">that Adam the first</t>
    <t s="25">(on the day he was created)</t>
    <t s="26">proclaimed to all the creations, "Come,</t>
    <t s="27">let us bow down and kneel, let us bend the knee before Hashem our Maker,"</t>
    <t s="28">and all answered and said, "Hashem</t>
    <t s="29">reigns, He is clothed in grandeur."</t>
    <t s="30">And this is that the seventh month</t>
    <t s="31">(in which man was created)</t>
    <t s="32">is the month of the oath,</t>
    <t s="33">for the power that man has to act upon the world,</t>
    <t s="34">even though in revelation man is after the act of Creation,</t>
    <t s="35">is through the revelation of man's true root,</t>
    <t s="36">which is before the act of Creation,</t>
    <t s="37">and this revelation is through the oath</t>
    <t s="38">(as explained at length above),</t>
    <t s="39">the month of the oath.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="11">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that on Rosh Hashanah each year, Israel coronates G-d, making the world a dwelling place, and this power comes from the renewed oath "be righteous," which was further revealed by the Alter Rebbe's discourse.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And similarly it is on Rosh Hashanah of each and every year,</t>
    <t s="1">for then Israel coronates</t>
    <t s="2">[who are called "man,"</t>
    <t s="3">for in each and every Jew there is a spark from the soul of Adam the first,</t>
    <t s="4">as above in section 3]</t>
    <t s="5">the Holy One, blessed be He, as King over themselves and over the entire world,</t>
    <t s="6">through which they make the world a dwelling place for Him, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="7">and in each and every year the coronation and the making of the dwelling place through this are in a more elevated manner,</t>
    <t s="8">for the power that each and every Jew has for this is through that on each Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="9">the beginning of the month of the oath,</t>
    <t s="10">the oath with which they adjure each and every Jew "be righteous" is drawn anew.</t>
    <t s="11">And it can be said,</t>
    <t s="12">that through the fact that the Alter Rebbe delivered the discourse of "They adjure him 'be righteous'" on Rosh Hashanah,</t>
    <t s="13">the utterance of Torah</t>
    <t s="14">(Torah Ohr),</t>
    <t s="15">the drawing down of the oath on Rosh Hashanah is in even greater revelation.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
